decision: Stop under the brief counterexample branch. Do not apply the generic endpoint-only cache to production. Fixed-geometry neutral equivalence is insufficient to guarantee original query answers through geometry mutation. This is not a theorem that all narrower native-only, explicitly invalidated reuse schemes are unsound.

sourceTrace.facts: worldQuery.segmentHitsBoatSolid delegates to segmentHitsShip. The latter reads ACTIVE, POSED positions, SIN/COS, SHIP_SPECS, precomputed REACH/TOP/SHIP_BOXES; local slab intersection uses scratch L but does not update ship geometry. Segment order and finite endpoint values matter. Static boxes derive from existing native fleet specs; no models changed.

setFleetState recomputes poses/headings/trigonometry from match time and sets team/platform masks. setShipStates separately updates ALIVE/SOLID, dropping collision at now-sunkAt>=20, then refreshes ACTIVE. fleetState exposes match time/team/platform fields, not a solidity generation. World object/function identity remains constant while answers change.

advance may execute several ticks. Each step synchronizes fleet before brain/movement work; spawn/deck paths also synchronize. Boat brains run before the sequential vehicle movement loop. Native ordinary geometry has no identified writer inside one uninterrupted stock movement invocation. Match time is0 in intermission while ship solidity still depends on advancing room time. A whole advance, world-object lifetime or fleetState tuple is not a general invalidation boundary.

Adapter calls the native solid oracle before testing conservative spheres of other boats. It captures filtered entity references, not immutable positions: sequential movement can change peer positions between boat invocations. Candidate only wraps the native oracle before this adapter; it does not cache combined peer contact results.

Client fleet synchronization and ship-state snapshot application write geography; reconciliation uses an adapter across several input-history entries. JavaScript movement calls are synchronous, so these source sites are not evidence of ordinary mid-call preemption. No browser/client execution occurred here.

The structural WorldQuery interface supplies callbacks without an immutable-geometry lease/revision. hullClear interleaves ground/water/bed reads and solid queries; movement retains current-pose/yaw/X/Z/buoyancy checks. AI invokes the same navigability predicate for course sampling. Generic per-movement caching cannot assume that every representable callback leaves native geometry unchanged.

counterexample.kind: declared reentrant WorldQuery geometry-hook fixture, not ordinary room execution
counterexample.change: setShipStates reactivates native carrier after water query342, between hull checks

output.limits: Ordinary fixed-geometry single-step equality is not a public WorldQuery purity/invalidation guarantee. The counterexample exercises a callback representable by the current interface with explicit native geometry updates; no claim that stock ordinary RoomEngine changes geometry mid-movement. No production cache, timing benefit/full-match share, score/reset/kill, event-stream, save, device or five-pilot acceptance established.

experiment.candidate: In-memory Map, freshly allocated per single1/60s movement invocation. Ordered six finite endpoint coordinates, signed zero retained, no spatial approximation or reversed-segment reuse. Misses delegate to original native query; hits reuse previous boolean. No cache is installed in production.
experiment.neutralComparison: One uncached and one candidate call from the same ordinary factory pose, native initial geography and four separated declared collider records. Full supplied boat state and complete logical ground/water/bed/solid answer order match; peer records remain unchanged. Actual native delegates6427->2980, reuses3447. No performance-speedup assertion: tracing/key/allocation overhead and warm-up are uncontrolled.
experiment.nativeBoundaryChecks: A point1cm inside the native carrier box changes hit true->false after one1/60s pose update. At fixed matchTime0/team2, native solidity changes true->false at age20s without changing fleetState tuple. These are isolated geometry fixtures, not observations of a live room clock or ship kill.
experiment.counterexample: A separate declared callback fixture starts with the native carrier non-solid and reactivates it via setShipStates after water query342. Both paths receive the identical update hook. Within the same movement invocation, logical query468 has identical endpoints but cache returnsfalse where uncached/fresh native returns true. Required ordered-query equivalence fails, although final boat states happen to match.
experiment.counterexampleLimits: This reentrant hook is representable by the current callback interface but is NOT stock ordinary RoomEngine ordering and is NOT evidence that the existing five-pilot run changes geometry mid-movement. Cross-boundary native probes do not alone disprove fresh per-call caching under a proved immutable native-only lease. That narrower production contract is not established or delivered by this generic candidate.
